transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I haven’t been handling things well since my daughter left for basic training. I come home and the house just feels dead, and I can’t seem to keep myself together.

I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts, messing up steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, snapping at the younger guys at work. And I’ve stopped doing the things I usually care about, like going out on the water or working on my sculpture. I just… don’t see the point lately.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?
It’s been about a month now, since she left. I’ve felt like this pretty much the whole time.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy or have you just not had the energy to do them?

It’s more that I’ve lost interest. I mean, I’m tired too, but even when I have the time, I don’t want to go out on the water or work on my sculpture. Those used to matter to me, and now I just look at them and think… what’s the point. Since my daughter left, the house feels so empty, and I just can’t get myself together.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about anything since your daughter left?
I don’t know if I’d call it worthless. I haven’t really been thinking that way. I feel bad, and I miss her a lot, but I’m not sitting there blaming myself for her leaving or anything like that.
Have you been feeling sad most of the day since your daughter left?

Yeah. Most days, yes. Since she left, I come home and the house just feels dead, and I can’t seem to keep myself together. I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts, and even at work I’m not right. It’s like it’s sitting on me most of the day.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Not really. I used to look forward to going out on the water, or working on my sculpture after work, but since my daughter left for basic training I just… don’t care about any of it. I come home and the house feels dead, and I look at those things and think, what’s the point.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide since your daughter left?
No… I mean, I’ve been really upset and overwhelmed, but I haven’t been thinking about killing myself or anything like that.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your daughter left?
I don’t know… I haven’t really been paying close attention to that. I guess I can’t say for sure if it’s changed in some big way.
Have you had more than two weeks of feeling sad most of the day?
Yeah… it’s been about a month now since my daughter left, and I’ve been feeling like this pretty much the whole time. So, yes, more than two weeks.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling restless and unable to sit still since your daughter left?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower or being unable to sit still, at least not in a way I can clearly point to.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since your daughter left?
I’m not sure. I haven’t been weighing myself or really paying attention to it, so I can’t say if my weight’s changed much.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating on things like work or reading since your daughter left?

Yes. At work especially. I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and that’s not like me. I’ll be standing there and my mind just… goes back to my daughter being gone. I’ve cried in the truck before shifts, and by the time I get inside I’m already not right. I can’t seem to keep myself together or stay focused.
Do you feel like your sadness is mild, or is it so severe that it's interfering with your daily life?

It’s severe. It’s not just feeling sad in the background. My supervisor actually took me off a complex welding job because I wasn’t coordinating safely enough, and I also let a sculpture submission pass without finishing it. So… yeah, it’s interfering with my life.
Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of pleasure?

Not really. I mean, I used to like going out on the water or working on my sculpture, but since my daughter left for basic training, I just don’t see the point. I come home and the house feels dead. I mostly just fall apart, or I’m trying to keep it together enough to get through work.
Are you unable to experience pleasure from activities that you normally find enjoyable?

Yeah. I can’t really get pleasure from the things I used to. I used to go out on the water, and I used to work on my sculpture, but since my daughter left for basic training, I just don’t see the point. I come home and the house feels dead, and I’m mostly just trying not to fall apart.
Do you feel like you've been fidgety or restless, or have you been feeling slowed down since your daughter left?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to that part. I don’t think I’ve been fidgety exactly, and I don’t know if I’d call it slowed down. I just… don’t feel right.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your daughter left?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been weighing myself, and I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting different or anything.
Do you feel like you've been moving slower than usual since your daughter left?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower exactly. I just feel off, but I can’t say if I’m actually slower than usual.
Do you feel like you've been moving slower than you usually do?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really noticed that I’m moving slower, not in a clear way. I just haven’t been paying close attention to it.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than usual or have trouble sitting still since your daughter left?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower, and I don’t think I’ve been especially restless either. I just haven’t paid much attention to that.
